questions.question: In branch-and-bound for an integer program, the LP relaxation of a node gives a fractional value $x_j=v$ for an integer variable, and the node is split into $x_j\le\lfloor v\rfloor$ and $x_j\ge\lceil v\rceil$. Why is this split safe?
options: The two children's LP values always average to the LP value of the node.
All integer solutions of the node survive, and the fractional value is cut off.
The optimal integer solution always lies in the child with the larger LP bound.
Each child's LP relaxation then has an integral optimum, which ends the branching.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for an integer program in $x_1,x_2$, the root was split on $x_2$; the child with $x_2\le1$ was then split on $x_1$, creating a node with $x_1\ge4$. Which constraints does this node's LP relaxation add to the original constraints?
options: Only $x_1\ge4$, its own branch
Both $x_1\ge4$ and $x_2\ge2$
$x_1\ge4$, $x_2\le1$ and integrality of $x_1,x_2$
Both $x_2\le1$ and $x_1\ge4$

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, a node's LP relaxation has optimal value 17.4. What does 17.4 say about the integer-feasible solutions that satisfy this node's branching constraints?
options: None of them has an objective value above 17.4.
None of them has an objective value below 17.4.
The best of them has objective value exactly 17.4.
Nothing, since only the root LP value bounds any solution.

questions.question: Two analysts solve the same integer program by branch-and-bound. When several variables are fractional, one always branches on the first fractional variable and the other on the last. Both run the method correctly to completion. How do their results compare?
options: Their optimal values may differ with the choice.
Same optimal value; tree sizes may differ.
Only one rule gives a proven optimal value.
Same optimal value and the very same tree.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, the LP relaxation of some node, not the root, has an optimal solution in which every integer variable takes an integer value. What follows for this node?
options: It is optimal for the whole integer program, so all other nodes can be closed.
It is the best integer solution of this node, so the node needs no branching.
The node must still be split on each variable to confirm the value is integral.
Its value is only a lower bound for this node, so the node is split further.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for an integer program, the LP relaxation of the current node gives the integer variable $x_1$ the value $2.7$. Which two child subproblems are created by branching on $x_1$?
options: $x_1\le3$ and $x_1\ge3$
$x_1=3$ only, the rounded value
$x_1\le2$ and $x_1\ge3$

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a binary integer program, the LP relaxation of a node, with $0\le x_3\le1$ in place of $x_3\in\{0,1\}$, gives $x_3=0.4$. Which two children are created by branching on $x_3$?
options: $x_3=0$ only

questions.question: A mixed integer program requires $x$ to be an integer and lets $y\ge0$ be continuous. In branch-and-bound, a node's LP relaxation has optimal solution $x=3$, $y=2.5$. What does branch-and-bound do at this node?
options: Branch on $y$ into the children $y\le2$ and $y\ge3$.
Round $y$ to 3 and record that solution instead.
No branching, since $x=3$ already is an integer.
Branch on $x$ and $y$, since both appear in the LP.

questions.question: Branch-and-bound is applied to the integer program: maximize $x_1+3x_2$ subject to $2x_1+5x_2\le12$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ integer. The root LP relaxation gives $(x_1,x_2)=(0,2.4)$. What happens to the child with the branch constraint $x_2\ge3$?
options: It stays open with the root's LP value 7.2 as its bound.
It is split on $x_1$ until an integer point appears.
Its point is rounded down to $x_2=2$ and added to the tree.
It is closed, since $x_2\ge3$ forces $2x_1+5x_2\ge15>12$.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, the best integer-feasible objective value found so far is 20. An unexplored node has LP relaxation value 19.5 at a fractional point. What should be done with this node?
options: Branch on it, since its LP solution is still fractional.
Keep it, since 19.5 rounds up to 20 and may tie.
Discard it: no integer solution in it can beat 20.
Use 19.5 as the new best value, since it is newer.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for a maximization integer program, a parent node has LP relaxation value 21. A child is formed by adding one branching constraint, and its LP relaxation is feasible. What must hold for the child's LP value?
options: It is at most 21, as the child's feasible set is inside the parent's.
It is at least 21, since the added constraint pushes the value upwards.
It equals 21, since the objective function has not changed at all.
It can be above or below 21, depending on the branching variable.

questions.question: Branch-and-bound is applied to a maximization integer program. At which moment has the best integer-feasible solution found so far been proved optimal?
options: When no unresolved node has an LP bound above its value.
As soon as the first integer-feasible node has been found.
As soon as the root LP relaxation has been solved.
Once every variable has been branched on at least once.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound for an integer program with general integer variable $x_1\ge0$, a node was created with $x_1\le3$. Deeper below it, an LP relaxation gives $x_1=2.5$. How does branch-and-bound handle $x_1$ there?
options: It may not branch on $x_1$ again anywhere on this path.
It branches on $x_1$ again: $x_1\le2$ and $x_1\ge3$.
It must branch on another variable instead.
It sets $x_1=3$, the bound from the ancestor.

questions.question: Branch-and-bound is applied to: maximize $5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $6x_1+4x_2\le24$, $x_1+2x_2\le6$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ integer. The root LP optimum is $(3,1.5)$ with value 21. What are the LP values of the children $x_2\le1$ and $x_2\ge2$?
options: 19 and 18
21 and 21

questions.question: For a maximization integer program, branch-and-bound gives root LP value 21. After the root is split, one child has an integral LP optimum with value 18 and the other has a fractional LP optimum with value $62/3\approx20.67$. Which bounds on the optimal value $z^*$ follow from these numbers alone?
options: $z^*=18$ exactly

questions.question: A minimization integer program is being solved by branch-and-bound. The cheapest integer-feasible solution found so far costs 50, and an open node's LP relaxation has optimal value 48.5 at a fractional point. Should this node be discarded or explored?
options: Discard it, since its value 48.5 is lower than 50.
Discard it, since its LP optimum is fractional.
Accept 48.5 as the new optimal cost of the program.
Explore it, as a cost below 50 may still lie in it.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound, suppose each new node kept only its own branching constraint and dropped those of its ancestors (for example, a node created by $x_1\ge4$ below a $x_2\le1$ branch would keep $x_1\ge4$ only). Why does this break the method?
options: The method is still correct but it needs a few more nodes.
Every LP relaxation becomes infeasible once ancestors are dropped.
The nodes no longer split the region, so cut-off points return.
Nothing changes, because the parent's LP optimum is already known.

questions.question: In branch-and-bound, a node's LP optimum has $x_1=3$ (integral) and $x_2=1.6$ (fractional), with both variables required to be integers. A student splits the node on $x_1$ into $x_1\le3$ and $x_1\ge3$. What is wrong with this split?
options: Nothing, since any integer variable may be used to branch.
The child $x_1\ge3$ is infeasible, so a solution is lost.
Both children still contain the parent's optimum $(3,1.6)$.
Integer solutions with $x_1=3$ are cut off by the split.

questions.question: For: maximize $5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $6x_1+4x_2\le24$, $x_1+2x_2\le6$, $x_1,x_2\ge0$ integer, branch-and-bound gives the child $x_2\ge2$ the integral LP optimum $(2,2)$ with value 18, and the child $x_2\le1$ the LP optimum $(10/3,1)$ with value $62/3$. What is the optimal value of the integer program?

Branch-and-bound is applied to: maximize $8x_1+11x_2+6x_3$ subject to $5x_1+7x_2+4x_3\le14$, $x_j\in\{0,1\}$. The child $x_3=0$ has integral LP optimum $(1,1,0)$ with value 19; the child $x_3=1$ has LP value $14+55/7\approx21.86$ at a fractional point. Which statement about the child $x_3=1$ is correct?
options: It holds an integer solution worth about 21.86.
It is discarded, since 19 is integral and optimal now.
It must be explored, yet may hold nothing above 19.
It is discarded, since its LP optimum is fractional.
